title: FINTRAC suspicious transaction indicators
text: Rapid increases in transaction frequency, especially when paired with new counterparties or unusual channels, can indicate suspicious velocity patterns that merit review against the customer's expected profile.

title: Cross-border concentration review
text: A concentration of outgoing cross-border wires to a small number of jurisdictions or counterparties can elevate AML risk, particularly when the behaviour is inconsistent with customer segment and historical activity.

title: Round amount structuring style indicators
text: Repeated round amount cash or transfer activity near internal review thresholds can resemble structuring style behaviour. Analysts should consider frequency, timing, channel, and legitimate business context.

title: Model reconstruction error explanation
text: High reconstruction error means observed behaviour is poorly represented by the model's learned normal pattern. It is not proof of suspicious activity and should be explained with top contributing features and data quality checks.

title: Counterparty network concentration
text: Network concentration occurs when a high proportion of value or transaction count flows through one counterparty or tightly connected group. Review ownership, relationship evidence, geography, and transaction purpose.

title: Feature critique for AML models
text: AML feature critique should test stability, leakage, explainability, missingness, segmentation bias, and whether features align to known typologies rather than only optimizing predictive performance.
